newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH says no reply yet from British.
newsitem.headline: LVMH says no reply yet from British.

text.p: LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault's resignation from the board of Guinness does not signal that the British group definitively turned down his plan to merge LVMH's wine and spirits business with those of Guinness and Grand Metropolitan, an LVMH spokeswoman said on Monday.
"There hasn't been a definitive answer from the British," she told Reuters.

The British companies, which announced plans to merge in May, are expected to reply this week, possibly on Wednesday, to Arnault's alternative proposal for a three-way drinks merger, according to the French press.

The newspaper Les Echos said Arnault would travel to London on Wednesday to push his proposal to analysts and portfolio managers. It said he will argue that his plan would generate three billion sterling ($5 billion) in savings, compared with two billion sterling from a merger of Guinness and GrandMet.
Brokerage Ferri said he was expected to detail his proposal this week. "The LVMH boss has made it clear he was willing to take less than 35 percent of the new group," it said in a stock comment.

His stake in a merged drinks entity had been considered one of the sticking points, as many analysts estimated that LVMH's 66 percent stake in Moet Hennessy, his 14.2 percent stake in Guinness and 6.4 percent in GrandMet did not entitle him to 35 percent of the three companies' combined drinks businesses.
A source close to the deal indicated that LVMH was flexible on that point, depending on the valuation estimates presented by the British groups.

In a statement announcing Arnault's resignation from Guinness's board, LVMH repeated that his proposal, entailing de-mergers of the GrandMet and Guinness food and beer activities, would create more value for all the shareholders.
Guinness chairman Tony Greener quit LVMH's board in May shortly after the announcement of the Guinness-GrandMet merger which LVMH opposed from the start.
Arnault, disappointed with the return on LVMH's stake in Guinness, had been pushing its one-time British ally for a merger of their drinks businesses. ($ = 0.595 British Pounds Sterling)
